# About this document

This is a data dictionary for `summaryABSK_AllData`, the pixel-level table
returned by `dataPrepWrapper()`
([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)).
It describes each column, where it comes from, and how it was derived.

The data object documented here is the cached build
`` `r dataCacheId` `` in [`analyses/cacheNEW`](../analyses/cacheNEW). It has
`r format(nrow(summaryABSK_AllData), big.mark = ",")` rows (one per 30 m pixel),
`r ncol(summaryABSK_AllData)` columns, and
`r uniqueN(summaryABSK_AllData$FIRE_NAME)` fires
(`r paste(summaryABSK_AllData[, .(n = uniqueN(FIRE_NAME)), by = Province][, paste(n, Province)], collapse = ", ")`).

# About the data

The majority of the dataset was initially compiled by Colin Ferster and published in [Ferster et al. (2026)](http://www.mdpi.com/1999-4907/7/9/187),
and then treated and cleaned by Ceres Barros - Barros et al (in prep.). Departures from the Ferster et al. (2016) dataset are:

- Vegetation inventories: Alberta and Saskatchewan pre-fire vegetation inventories were standardized using the CASFRI (Common Attribute Schema for Forest Resource Inventories; Cosco 2011) standard.

- A continuous fire severity variable was created from the initial a categorical variable taking the mean percentage value of each severity class.

- Weather values were summarised in multiple ways (across full weather period, only the first 3 days, or taking the values of the first day), before finally settling into summaries across the first 3 days of each fire -- which provided better relationships with severity.

Sources of information about the original data are in the following files (in addition to code documentation.)

| Source | Location |
|---|---|
| Dave Andison's variable descriptions | [`data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx`](../data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx), [`data/fires_Dave/*/*_varCorresp.txt`](../data/fires_Dave) |
| Topography variable names | [`data/fires_Dave/DEM/DEMvars_cf_27Nov2018_CB.xlsx`](../data/fires_Dave/DEM/DEMvars_cf_27Nov2018_CB.xlsx), [`data/fires_Dave/DEM/README.txt`](../data/fires_Dave/DEM/README.txt) |
| Fire weather metadata | [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/README.txt`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/README.txt), [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations/interp_varlisting.txt`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations/interp_varlisting.txt), [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode/*.csv`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode) |
| Vegetation inventory conversion | [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx), [CAS_Document_Final_Mar_2010_ALL_APPENDICES.pdf][casman] (CASFRI manual; Appendix 2 data dictionary, Appendix 14 wetland codes), [`data/VegInventories/*_varCorresp.txt`](../data/VegInventories) |

# Data processing overview

The preparation runs in this order (functions in parentheses):

1. **Severity polygons** (AB1, AB2 and SK shapefiles in [`data/fires_Dave/fireSev`](../data/fires_Dave/fireSev)) are read and their severity classes harmonised (`cleanAndBindFireData()`).

2. **Fire events** are defined with a 200 m buffer, giving disturbed patches and inner and outer residual patches (`defineFireEvents()`; see also Andison & McCleary, 2014).

3. **Pre-fire vegetation polygons** (AVI and SFVI inventories in [`data/fires_Dave/prefireVeg`](../data/fires_Dave/prefireVeg)) are converted to CASFRI attributes (`ABToCASFRI()`, `SKToCASFRI()`).

4. **Fire weather** is read (`prepFireWeather()`) from the Large Fire Database 21-day interpolations from weather station data in `all129-overview.xls`. **Ecozones and natural regions** are also contained in this dataset.

5. Everything is **joined at 30 m pixels**: all polygon data (vegetation inventories and fire severity) is rasterized using a one cell-centre point per pixel using a 30m resolution grid ([`data/fires_Dave/DEM/Grid30Intersect`](../data/fires_Dave/DEM/Grid30Intersect)); topographic data layers are re-projected to the same resolutions. Severity, vegetation and topography data are joined spatially, and then joined by fire name to weather (`joinSevVegTopoWeatherData()`) -- note that fire waether data is a-spatial.

6. Weather is **summarised over days 1-3**.

7. Overstorey layer of vegetation data is kept, with added an added binary variable of "understory"; species are reshaped to one column each (`summarizeABSK_AllData()`) then collapsed by fire-functional types -- flammable conifers, tamarack, deciduous and firs (`dataPrepWrapper()`).

7. **Final clean-ups** : non-forest land-cover types and wetlands are recoded into a single land cover variable; several `NA`s are filled to avoid data loss, and a proportional (0 to 1) severity variable is created (`SEV_PROP`).


## Data structure and other metadata

- **Resolution:** 30 m. `dataPrepWrapper(resolution = 30)` is passed
  to the join.
- **Projection:** the CRS of the severity shapefiles
  ([`data/fires_Dave/fireSev/*.prj`](../data/fires_Dave/fireSev)), an Albers equal-area projection on NAD83
  (standard parallels 50° and 70°, latitude of origin 40°, central meridian
  −96°, units metres). The code takes the CRS from the severity data;
  it doesn't set one. Vegetation and topography layers are reprojected to it.
- **One row per pixel:** a raster is built over the extent of all severity
  polygons and each cell is numbered (`pixID`). For each fire,
  cells covered by the fire's polygons are kept, converted to cell-centre
  points, and the severity, vegetation and topography attributes at each point
  are attached by spatial joins. Fire weather is joined by fire
  name.
- **Vegetation layer:** only the top (overstorey) inventory layer is kept
  (`LAYER == 1`). The understorey only contributes the
  presence/absence flag `UNDERSTOREY`.

## Rows removed during preparation

| Step | Rows removed |
|---|---|
| AB2 water polygons | `FIRE_CODE == 9`^a^ |
| Event perimeter patches | `PatchType == "eventPerim"`^b^ |
| Cells not inside a fire's polygons | Cells outside the rasterised polygons^c^ |
| No severity polygon at the point | Unmatched points^c^ |
| No topography feature at the pixel | Unmatched pixels; fires outside the topography extent lose all pixels^c^ |
| No vegetation polygon at the point | Unmatched points^c^ |
| No fire weather for the fire | Unmatched fires^c^ |
| Non-overstorey layers | `LAYER != 1`^d^ |

Table: `r tabNum()`Rows removed during data preparation. ^a^ `cleanAndBindFireData()`, ^b^ `dataPrepWrapper()` (both in [`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^c^ `joinSevVegTopoWeatherData()` ([`R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R`](../R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R)), joins that drop unmatched rows (`nomatch = 0`); ^d^ `summarizeABSK_AllData()` ([`analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R`](../analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R)).

Columns that are all `NA` or all 0 are also dropped. This is why,
for example, `DIST3_*`, `STAND_STRUCTURE_PER` and `NUMBER_OF_LAYERS` are not
in the table.

# Variables

## Identifiers and location

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `pixID` | Pixel identifier | Cell number of the 30 m template raster covering all fires; unique across the study area.^a^ |
| `Long` | x coordinate of the pixel centre | Projected metres in the Albers CRS above, **not longitude in degrees**, despite the name.^a^ |
| `Lat` | y coordinate of the pixel centre | Projected metres, **not latitude in degrees**.^a^ |
| `gridID` | Identifier of the topography feature joined to the pixel | First column of the topography shapefiles, renamed.^b^ `r uniqueN(summaryABSK_AllData$gridID)` unique values for `r format(nrow(summaryABSK_AllData), big.mark = ",")` pixels, so some topography features cover several pixels. **Note:** this is the original topography (DEM) pixel ID (C. Barros). |
| `P_ID` | Pre-fire vegetation polygon identifier | Renumbered sequentially after binding the AB and SK inventories.^b^ Not the inventory's original polygon number: the original polygon IDs can't be trusted because several polygons share an ID.^c^ |

Table: `r tabNum()`Identifiers and location. ^a^ `joinSevVegTopoWeatherData()` ([`R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R`](../R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R)); ^b^ `ABSKfires_DataPrep()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^c^ D. Andison's notes in [`data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx`](../data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx).

## Fire attributes

All of these take one value per fire.

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `FIRE_NAME` | Fire name | From the severity shapefiles, field renamed using the correspondence files.^a,b^ Upper-cased; `Alfred` renamed `ALFRED LAKE`.^c^ Factor. |
| `FIRE_YEAR` | Fire year | From the severity shapefiles. AB2 codes `<1953`, `195X`, `194X` are recoded to 1953, 1952 and 1945, and several SK fires have years set by hand.^a^ **Note:** the hand-set years are adjustments provided by the data owner, D. Andison (pers. comm.), with reference to the fire overview table.^d^ |
| `Province` | Province | `"AB"` or `"SK"`, set according to the source shapefile.^a^ |
| `fireNum` | Fire number in the Large Fire Database (LFDB) weather files | Read from the fire-description lines of the LFDB weather files.^e^ ALGAR (and ALGARITA) reuse BASELINE's weather, and so share its `fireNum` (`r summaryABSK_AllData[FIRE_NAME %in% c("ALGAR", "BASELINE"), paste(unique(fireNum), collapse = ", ")]`). |
| `Czone1` | Canadian ecozone of the fire | From the fire overview table.^d^ Where `Czone1` is Boreal and `Czone2` is Montane, `Czone2` is used (Little Smoky and Gregg River fires).^f^ Follows the Canadian ecozone and ecoregion definitions. The level `Boreal PLain` is spelled as in the source. **Note:** not used in the models. |
| `NR1` | Alberta natural region of the fire | From the fire overview table.^d^ Set to `Foothills` where `NR2` is Foothills and `NR1` is neither Rocky nor Foothills (Livock fire).^f^ Follows the provincial natural regions classification (Alberta's). **Note:** SK fires are assigned the equivalent Alberta natural region (`Canadian Shield`, `Boreal Forest`) to avoid `NA`s. Not used in the models. |
| `Duration` | Fire duration | Taken as is from the fire duration table,^g^ not computed; in the rows checked it equals the stop minus the start date. `NA` for `r summaryABSK_AllData[is.na(Duration), uniqueN(FIRE_NAME)]` fires with no stop date. **Note:** units are days (C. Barros); they are not stated in the source file. |
| `Area` | Area | From the fire duration table,^g^ thousands separators removed; one value per fire. **Note:** legacy variable, not used; units unknown. |
| `Pre.` | `Pre?` column of the fire duration table^g^ | Imported as is; `Pre?` becomes `Pre.` on import. All values are `Yes` in this data. **Note:** legacy variable, not used; probably indicates that pre-fire vegetation data are available for the fire (C. Barros). |
| `startJulDay` | Day of year of the first day of the fire | First `julDay` of the summarised weather days (see Fire weather).^h^ **Note:** for 8 of 30 fires it differs from the start date in the fire overview file^i^ (1 to 4 days earlier for 7 fires, 30 days for DARIEU LAKE). `julDay` in Ferster's weather data is the first day of the fire and is the date used to compute the FWI System variables, so it is taken as authoritative. |

Table: `r tabNum()`Fire attributes. ^a^ `cleanAndBindFireData()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^b^ [`data/fires_Dave/fireSev/*Postfire_varCorresp.txt`](../data/fires_Dave/fireSev); ^c^ `joinSevVegTopoWeatherData()` ([`R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R`](../R/R_tools/joinSevVegTopoWeatherData.R)); ^d^ [`data/fires_Dave/all129-overview.xls`](../data/fires_Dave/all129-overview.xls), sheet `all`; ^e^ `prepFireWeather()` ([`R/R_tools/prepFireWeather.R`](../R/R_tools/prepFireWeather.R)), reading the `interp_*.tab` files in [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations); ^f^ `ABSKfires_DataPrep()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^g^ [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode/fireDuration.csv`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode/fireDuration.csv); ^h^ `summarizeABSK_AllData()` ([`analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R`](../analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R)); ^i^ [`data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode/Overview.csv`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeatherCode/Overview.csv).

## Fire severity (response)

Fire severity is post-fire vegetation mortality, interpreted from aerial
photography by one interpreter into six classes (manuscript, Fire severity
data). Mortality includes dead tree crowns in forested areas, dead shrubs, and
the area scorched in grass or bryophyte cover.

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `SEV_CLASS` | Severity class (increasing mortality) | AB2 (`FIRE_CODE`) and SK (`CLASS`) are already mortality classes 0-5. AB1 records percent **survival**, recoded as `100%`→0, `75-99%`→1, `50-74%`→2, `25-49%`→3, `6-24%`→4, `0-5%`→5.^a^ Residual patches (`inResids`, `outResids`) are set to 0.^b^ |
| `SEV_CONT` | Severity in percent mortality | Median of each class's range: 0, 13 (1-25), 38 (26-50), 63 (51-75), 85 (76-94), 97.5 (95-100).^a^ |
| `SEV_PROP` | Severity as a proportion (model response) | `SEV_CONT / 100`, with 0.975 set to **1**.^c^ |
| `PatchType` | Patch type within the fire event | The fire event perimeter is the union of a fire's polygons, buffered out by 200 m and back in.^d^ `disturbedPatch`: the mapped fire polygons. `inResids`: unburned patches inside the event perimeter connected to holes created by the buffering (inner residuals). `outResids`: other unburned areas inside the event perimeter. The manuscript describes this as following Andison (2014) to include fire islands. |

Table: `r tabNum()`Fire severity variables. ^a^ `cleanAndBindFireData()`, ^b^ `ABSKfires_DataPrep()`, ^c^ `dataPrepWrapper()` (all in [`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^d^ `defineFireEvents()` ([`R/R_tools/Useful_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/Useful_functions.R)).

```{r sevTable}
summaryABSK_AllData[, .N, by = .(SEV_CLASS, SEV_CONT, SEV_PROP)][order(SEV_CLASS)] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(tabNum(), "Severity coding and pixel counts"))
summaryABSK_AllData[, .N, by = .(PatchType, SEV_CLASS)][order(PatchType, SEV_CLASS)] |>
  dcast.data.table(PatchType ~ SEV_CLASS, value.var = "N", fill = 0) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(tabNum(), "Pixels by patch type (rows) and severity class (columns)"))
```

`disturbedPatch` pixels can also have `SEV_CLASS == 0` (mapped 0% mortality
within the fire polygons).

## Fire weather

**Source:** daily fire weather interpolated for the 21 days of weather lines
attached to each fire in the Canadian Large Fire Database (LFDB) files
`interp_50s.tab` to `interp_90s.tab`
([`data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations`](../data/fires_Dave/fireWeather/20DayInterpolations)). Each weather line holds
`julDay, temp, rh, ws, rain, ffmc, dmc, dc, isi, bui, fwi`
(`interp_varlisting.txt`). The manuscript describes them as daily weather
averaged from station measurements during the first 21 days following
ignition, with the Canadian Fire Weather Index (FWI) System codes and indices
(Ferster et al. 2016; Amiro et al. 2001). Only AB and SK fires are kept, and
weather is linked to fire names through `fire_weather.dbf`.

**Days summarised:** for each fire, the distinct `julDay` values are sorted
and numbered, and the first three are kept (`days = 1:3`). All weather columns therefore summarise **the first three days**
of each fire, starting on the first day of the fire (see `startJulDay`).

**Statistics:** per pixel over those days. Values are constant
within a fire. `mean`, `min` and `max` are as named; `cv = sd(x) / mean(x)`,
with `sd` computed from at most three values; `range = max - min`.

| Variable stem | Variable | Unit (manuscript Table 1) |
|---|---|---|
| `Temp` | Air temperature. **Note:** `rangeTemp` was missing from earlier builds because of a bug (`rangeRH` was computed in its place);^a^ fixed on 2026-11-13 (commit `d9f0784`), and the data was rebuilt under the same `cacheId`, so this build includes `rangeTemp`. | °C |
| `RH` | Relative humidity | % |
| `WS` | Wind speed | km/h |
| `Rain` | Precipitation | mm |
| `FFMC` | Fine Fuel Moisture Code | unitless |
| `DMC` | Duff Moisture Code | unitless |
| `DC` | Drought Code | unitless |
| `ISI` | Initial Spread Index | unitless |
| `BUI` | Buildup Index | unitless |
| `FWI` | Fire Weather Index | unitless |

Table: `r tabNum()`Fire-weather variable stems. Each stem is summarised as `mean`, `min`, `max`, `cv` and `range` over the first three days of each fire (e.g. `meanTemp`, `cvFWI`); units from the manuscript's Table 1. ^a^ `summarizeABSK_AllData()` ([`analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R`](../analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R)).

The table contains `mean`, `min`, `max`, `cv` and `range` for each stem
(e.g. `meanTemp`, `cvFWI`, `rangeDC`). Notes:

- **`cvRain` is NA** for `r format(sum(is.na(summaryABSK_AllData$cvRain)), big.mark = ",")` pixels, all with `meanRain == 0` (0/0).

Units are as given in the manuscript's Table 1. The LFDB files and the code
don't state units, so the manuscript is the only source for them.

## Topography

**Source:** shapefiles `alta24.shp`, `alta77_revise.shp` and `sask29.shp` in
[`data/fires_Dave/DEM/Grid30Intersect`](../data/fires_Dave/DEM/Grid30Intersect). The README says the variables were
computed with the ArcGIS Gradient Metrics Toolbox (Evans); Ferster et al.
(2016) report using the Toolbox for Surface Gradient and Geomorphometric
Modeling, version 2.0-0, for ArcGIS 10.3.1. The original
data preparation is in `topo_names.R` in Colin Ferster's DEM folder (not in
this repo). Columns are renamed by position using the correspondence in
`DEMvars_cf_27Nov2018_CB.xlsx`, reprojected to the severity CRS,
and attached to pixels with `prioritizr::fast_extract()`. The
manuscript says the DEM had 30 m resolution.

| Variable | Description^a^ | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Elevation` | Elevation (m) | Original layer name `Smoo` / `Sm_1`. |
| `Aspect` | Aspect | Degrees (manuscript). **Note:** should not be used. `r round(100 * summaryABSK_AllData[, mean(Aspect == -117)], 1)`% of pixels have the undocumented code `-117`, which behaves like a flat-surface code (those pixels have near-zero `SCOS`/`SSIN`), but 40% of them have `PctSlope > 0`. Aspect is also circular, so `SCOS`/`SSIN` are the usable alternatives. |
| `PctSlope` | Slope percent (rise/run) | % |
| `DegSlope` | Slope degrees | Monotonic transform of `PctSlope` (ρ = 1.00).^b^ |
| `SCOS` | Slope × cos(aspect) | Slope-weighted northness. |
| `SSIN` | Slope × sin(aspect) | Slope-weighted eastness. |
| `CTI` | Compound Topographic Index | Soil wetness index (manuscript). |
| `Curv` | Curvature | |
| `SlopePosition` | Slope position | Correlates ρ = 0.99 with `Curv`. **Note:** toolbox parameters (e.g. window size) are not reported by Ferster et al. (2016) and are unknown; see below. |
| `SurfReliefRatio` | Surface Relief Ratio | Terrain roughness (manuscript). |
| `SurfAspectRatio` | Surface Aspect Ratio | The manuscript calls it terrain roughness, computed as area/cos(slope). In this data it equals 537.85 × sec(slope) exactly,^b^ so it carries no information beyond slope. |
| `TRASP` | Topographic Radiation Aspect Index | |

Table: `r tabNum()`Topographic variables. ^a^ [`data/fires_Dave/DEM/DEMvars_cf_27Nov2018_CB.xlsx`](../data/fires_Dave/DEM/DEMvars_cf_27Nov2018_CB.xlsx), unless noted; "(manuscript)" refers to the manuscript's Table 1; ^b^ [`analyses/DAfires_collinearityCheck.Rmd`](../analyses/DAfires_collinearityCheck.Rmd).

The toolbox settings (e.g. moving-window sizes) are not reported, either in
Ferster et al. (2016) or in this repo, so they are unknown for all topography
variables.

## Pre-fire vegetation

**Source:** pre-fire vegetation polygons interpreted from aerial photographs
taken within five years before the fire, following the Alberta Vegetation
Inventory (AVI) or the Saskatchewan Forest Vegetation Inventory (SFVI)
standards (manuscript). Inventory fields were renamed using
[`data/VegInventories/*_varCorresp.txt`](../data/VegInventories) and converted to the Common Attribute
Schema for Forest Resource Inventories (CASFRI; Cosco 2011) with
`ABToCASFRI()` and `SKToCASFRI()`. Code tables are in
[`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx). Attribute definitions below come
from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 2), unless noted.

In the conversion, CASFRI missing and error codes are set to `NA`, so missing and erroneous inventory values can't be told apart.
Afterwards, `dataPrepWrapper()` fills many `NA`s for non-forest pixels with 0
or with labels such as `"notDisturbed"`; see each variable.

"Derivation and coding" columns refer to the provincial vegetation inventory fields as "AB" or "SK".

Table: `r tabNum()`Tree species columns, in percent of overstorey species composition. AVI and SFVI codes from the `SpeciesTable` sheet of [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx).

Codes from the `SpeciesTable` sheet of `CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`. Species in
that table but not in the data (e.g. *Pinus albicaulis*) are not columns
because they don't occur in the overstorey of these fires.

- **Units:** percent of overstorey species composition, in 10% steps. The
  inventory value (tenths) is multiplied by 10 (`spPercent()`).
  The [CASFRI manual][casman] defines species percentages as "percent species
  composition in 10% increments".
- **Derivation:** the inventory's species slots (`SPEC1..n`, `SPEC1_PER..n`)
  of the overstorey layer are reshaped to one column per species, summed per
  pixel. Per pixel, the 11 species sum to 100 on forested pixels
  and to 0 on non-forested pixels (`DAfires_collinearityCheck.Rmd`).
- **NA filling:** `NA` → 0.
- **Note: code issue fixed 2026-11-16, no effect on this data.** `spPercentAdjust()`
  is meant to correct AB compositions whose species percentages don't sum to
  100. Its AB branch used comparisons (`sppPer[1] == 60`) where assignments
  (`sppPer[1] <- 60`) were intended, so it returned the percentages
  unchanged. In this data every AB and SK pixel sums to exactly 0 or 100, so
  the correction cases don't occur in the overstorey records used here, and
  the cache was not rebuilt after the fix.

### Species groups

| Variable | Description | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| `FlamConif` | Flammable conifers, % | `Pice glau + Pice mari + Pice enge + Pinu cont + Pinu bank` |
| `Abie` | Firs, % | `Abie bals + Abie lasi` |
| `Decid` | Broadleaf/deciduous species, % (`Broadleaf` in the manuscript) | `Popu trem + Popu balb + Betu papy` |
| `Lari` | Tamarack, % | `Lari lari` (renamed; kept as its own group) |

Table: `r tabNum()`Species groups, in percent of overstorey species composition, computed in `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)).

`FlamConif + Abie + Lari + Decid` = 100 on
forested pixels and 0 elsewhere.

### Stand attributes

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `HEIGHT_UPPER`, `HEIGHT_LOWER` | Upper and lower bound of average stand height of dominant and co-dominant trees | AB: `HEIGHT` ± 0.5 when 0 < `HEIGHT` ≤ 50; SK: ± 0.5 when 0 < `HEIGHT` ≤ 100.^a^ Metres.^b^ `NA` → 0.^c^ **Note:** the two columns always differ by exactly 1 m (± 0.5 m around the recorded height), so one of them is redundant for modelling. |
| `CROWN_CLOSURE_UPPER`, `CROWN_CLOSURE_LOWER` | Upper and lower bound of crown closure class: percentage of ground covered by the vertical projection of crowns | AB: `DENSITY` class A/B/C/D → lower 6/31/51/71, upper 30/50/70/100.^d^ SK: `CROWN_CLOSURE` (0-100) used for both bounds.^a^ `NA` → 0.^c^ **Note:** for SK, the two bounds are identical, because the SFVI records a single crown-closure percentage; for AB, they differ, giving the bounds of the AVI density class. |
| `ORIGIN_UPPER`, `ORIGIN_LOWER` | Upper and lower bound of stand origin (establishment) year | AB: 4-digit years kept; 2-digit decade codes `YY` → `1YY9` (upper) and `1YY0` (lower); years < 1600 or > 2014 → `NA`. SK: years ending in 0 get +5 (upper) or −4 (lower).^a^ `NA` → 0,^c^ so 0 means unknown or non-forest, not a year. **Note:** for AB, the two bounds are identical where the AVI records a single origin year. |
| `STAND_AGE` | Stand age at the time of the fire, years | `FIRE_YEAR − ORIGIN_UPPER` when `ORIGIN_UPPER` is not `NA`; `NA` → 0.^c^ **Note:** unreliable; not used in the models. `r summaryABSK_AllData[STAND_AGE < 0, format(.N, big.mark = ",")]` forested pixels have negative ages (minimum `r min(summaryABSK_AllData$STAND_AGE)`), i.e. a stand origin after the fire year, and `NA` origins are filled with 0. |
| `STAND_STRUCTURE` | Vertical organisation of layers: S = single-layered, M = multi-layered, C = complex, H = horizontal | AB: `STRUC`; SK: `LAYER_TYPE`, with `NA` → `S`.^a,d^ Remaining `NA` → `S`.^c^ All SK pixels are `S`. **Note:** the rule that assigns `M` to multi-layered stands with missing structure runs after only layer 1 is kept, so it likely never applies; accepted (C. Barros). |
| `SITE_CLASS` | Site productivity class: U = unproductive, P = poor, M = medium, G = good | AB: `TPR` (U→U, F→P, M→M, G→G).^a,d^ SK inventories have no equivalent, so all SK pixels are `unknown`. `NA` → `"unknown"`.^c^ |
| `UNDERSTOREY` | Presence of a tree understorey | `TRUE` if the pixel's layer-2 record has any species cover; `NA` → `FALSE`. Only AB layer 2 is considered.^e^ The understorey "can't really be trusted (Andison pers. comm. January 29th 2019)", because aerial photos can miss it.^e^ |
| `LAYER`, `LAYER_RANK` | CASFRI layer number and rank | `LAYER_RANK` equals `LAYER`.^a^ Always 1 after the overstorey filter.^e^ |

Table: `r tabNum()`Stand attributes. Descriptions from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 2). ^a^ `ABToCASFRI()` / `SKToCASFRI()` ([`R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R)); ^b^ manuscript; the AVI and SFVI descriptions in [`data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx`](../data/fires_Dave/Variable_description.xlsx) say height is recorded to the nearest metre; ^c^ `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^d^ conversion tables (`CrownClos*Table`, `StandStructTable`, `SiteClass` sheets) in [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx); ^e^ `summarizeABSK_AllData()` ([`analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R`](../analyses/R_tools/summarizeABSK_AllData.R)), code and comments.

### Soil moisture

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `SMR` | Soil moisture regime (CASFRI): D = dry, F = mesic/fresh, M = moist, W = wet, A = aquatic | AB: AVI `d`→D, `m`→F, `w`→W, `a`→A; `n`/`u` → W if the leading species is tamarack, otherwise M.^a^ SK: VD, D → D; MF, F, VF → F; MM, M, VM → M; MW, W, VW → W.^b^ Non-forest pixels with missing SMR: land cover WA, RI, OC, LA, SI, TF, LG → A; FL → W. Remaining `NA` → `"unknown"`.^c^ **Note:** AVI `m` (mesic) maps to CASFRI `F` (fresh/mesic), not CASFRI `M` (moist), following the CASFRI convention (the code is a translation of the CASFRI Perl scripts, and codes are upper-cased first), so CASFRI `M` only arises from AVI `n`/`u` codes. |
| `SMR_ord` | `SMR` as an ordered variable | D=1, F=2, M=3, W=4, A=5; `unknown` → `NA`.^c^ |
| `SMR_wet` | Wet or aquatic soil | `TRUE` if `SMR_ord` is 4 or 5; `NA` if `SMR_ord` is `NA`.^c^ |

Table: `r tabNum()`Soil moisture variables. Descriptions from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 2). ^a^ `soilMoistureRegime()` ([`R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R)); ^b^ `SMRTable` sheet of [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx); ^c^ `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)).

### Disturbance history

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `DIST1`, `DIST2` | Type of earlier disturbance recorded in the inventory | BU = burn, CO = cut, DI = disease, DT = dead tops/trees, OT = other.^a^ AB: from `MOD1`/`MOD2`; SK: from `DISTURBANCE_1`/`_2`. In AB, `ANTH_NON == "AIL"` is coded `CO` with extent 95-100%.^b^ `NA` → `"notDisturbed"`.^c^ |
| `DIST1_EXTENT_LOWER`, `DIST1_EXTENT_UPPER`, `DIST2_EXTENT_LOWER`, `DIST2_EXTENT_UPPER` | Lower and upper bounds of disturbance extent class (%) | Lower bounds 1/26/51/76/96 and upper bounds 25/50/75/95/100 for extent classes 1-5.^a^ `NA` → 0.^c^ |
| `DIST1_YEAR`, `DIST2_YEAR` | Year of disturbance | Always 0 in this data (no years recorded; `NA` → 0).^c^ These columns are not dropped by the all-0 rule because it runs before the `NA` filling. **Note:** the AB disturbance-year range check used `&` (`< 1880 & > 2020`), so it could never be true;^b^ fixed to `|` on 2026-11-16, with no effect on this data. |

Table: `r tabNum()`Disturbance history variables. Descriptions from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 2). ^a^ `DisturbanceTable`, `DistExtLowerTable` and `DistExtUpperTable` sheets of [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx); ^b^ `ABToCASFRI()` / `SKToCASFRI()` ([`R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R)); ^c^ `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)).

### Land cover and wetlands

| Variable | Description | Derivation and coding |
|---|---|---|
| `LandCover` | Land-cover type | The CASFRI non-forest attributes `NATURALLY_NON_VEG`, `NON_FORESTED_VEG` and `NON_FORESTED_ANTHRO` are merged. Pixels with none of these and not a non-treed wetland are considered forested and labelled "productive forest", `PF` (to avoid having two forested classes). Wetland pixels get a suffix `_wet_<WETLAND_CLASS>` (e.g. `PF_wet_S`), or `wet_<WETLAND_CLASS>` if they have no land-cover code.^a^ |
| `isForest` | Forested pixel | `TRUE` when there is no non-forest land-cover code, except wetlands whose vegetation modifier is not F (forested) or T (treed).^a^ Equivalent to `LandCover` starting with `PF`. |
| `WETLAND_CLASS` | CASFRI wetland class: B = bog, F = fen, S = swamp, M = marsh, W = wetland (no distinction) | AB: derived from SMR, crown density, non-forest type and species.^b^ SK: derived from stand type.^c^ `NA` → `"notWetland"`.^a^ |
| `WETLAND_VEG_MOD` | Wetland vegetation modifier: F = forested, T = treed, O = not treed, freshwater | As above; `"notWetland"` for non-wetlands. |
| `WETLAND_LAND_MOD` | Wetland landform modifier: N = no permafrost or patterning | As above. **Note:** `-` appears for SK `W` wetlands (from the SK conversion of stand type `TMS`); it comes from the CASFRI Perl conversion code for SK and is kept as is. |
| `WETLAND_LOCAL_MOD` | Wetland local modifier: N = lawns not present, G = graminoids with shrub cover < 25%, S = shrub cover > 25% | As above. **Note:** `-` as for `WETLAND_LAND_MOD`. |

Table: `r tabNum()`Land cover and wetland variables. Wetland codes from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 14). ^a^ `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^b^ `wetlandCodesAB()`, ^c^ `wetlandCodesSK2()` (both in [`R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R)).

```{r lcTable}
summaryABSK_AllData[, .N, by = .(LandCover, isForest)][order(-N)] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(tabNum(), "Land-cover codes, forest status and pixel counts"))
```

| Code | Meaning | CASFRI attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `PF` | "Productive" forest (not a CASFRI code)^a^ | — |
| `LA` | Lake | `NATURALLY_NON_VEG` |
| `RI` | River | `NATURALLY_NON_VEG` |
| `BR` | Bryoid | `NON_FORESTED_VEG` |
| `HG` | Herbs, graminoids | `NON_FORESTED_VEG` |
| `SL` | Low shrub (shrub height < 2 m)^b^ | `NON_FORESTED_VEG` |
| `ST` | Tall shrub (shrub height ≥ 2 m)^b^ | `NON_FORESTED_VEG` |
| `FA` | Facility/infrastructure | `NON_FORESTED_ANTHRO` |
| `IN` | Industrial | `NON_FORESTED_ANTHRO` |
| `wet_*` | Wetland without another land-cover code | — |

Table: `r tabNum()`Land-cover codes, from the [CASFRI manual][casman] (Appendix 2) and the conversion tables in [`data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx`](../data/VegInventories/CASFRIConvTables.xlsx). ^a^ assigned in `dataPrepWrapper()` ([`analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R`](../analyses/R_tools/DAfires_dataPrep.R)); ^b^ shrub height threshold applied in `ABToCASFRI()` ([`R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R`](../R/R_tools/CASFRIrelated_functions.R)).

# Full column list

```{r fullList}
## categories and order follow the Variables sections above
weatherStems <- c("Temp", "RH", "WS", "Rain", "FFMC", "DMC", "DC", "ISI", "BUI", "FWI")
weatherStats <- c("mean", "min", "max", "cv", "range")
varCategories <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(Category = "Identifiers and location",
             Variable = c("pixID", "Long", "Lat", "gridID", "P_ID")),
  data.table(Category = "Fire attributes",
             Variable = c("FIRE_NAME", "FIRE_YEAR", "Province", "fireNum", "Czone1",
                          "NR1", "Duration", "Area", "Pre.", "startJulDay")),
  data.table(Category = "Fire severity",
             Variable = c("SEV_CLASS", "SEV_CONT", "SEV_PROP", "PatchType")),
  data.table(Category = "Fire weather",
             Variable = CJ(stem = weatherStems, stat = weatherStats,
                           sorted = FALSE)[, paste0(stat, stem)]),
  data.table(Category = "Topography",
             Variable = c("Elevation", "Aspect", "PctSlope", "DegSlope", "SCOS", "SSIN",
                          "CTI", "Curv", "SlopePosition", "SurfReliefRatio",
                          "SurfAspectRatio", "TRASP")),
  data.table(Category = "Tree species composition",
             Variable = c("Abie bals", "Abie lasi", "Betu papy", "Lari", "Pice enge",
                          "Pice glau", "Pice mari", "Pinu bank", "Pinu cont",
                          "Popu balb", "Popu trem")),
  data.table(Category = "Species groups",
             Variable = c("FlamConif", "Abie", "Decid")),
  data.table(Category = "Stand attributes",
             Variable = c("HEIGHT_UPPER", "HEIGHT_LOWER", "CROWN_CLOSURE_UPPER",
                          "CROWN_CLOSURE_LOWER", "ORIGIN_UPPER", "ORIGIN_LOWER",
                          "STAND_AGE", "STAND_STRUCTURE", "SITE_CLASS", "UNDERSTOREY",
                          "LAYER", "LAYER_RANK")),
  data.table(Category = "Soil moisture",
             Variable = c("SMR", "SMR_ord", "SMR_wet")),
  data.table(Category = "Disturbance history",
             Variable = c("DIST1", "DIST2", "DIST1_EXTENT_LOWER", "DIST1_EXTENT_UPPER",
                          "DIST2_EXTENT_LOWER", "DIST2_EXTENT_UPPER", "DIST1_YEAR",
                          "DIST2_YEAR")),
  data.table(Category = "Land cover and wetlands",
             Variable = c("LandCover", "isForest", "WETLAND_CLASS", "WETLAND_VEG_MOD",
                          "WETLAND_LAND_MOD", "WETLAND_LOCAL_MOD"))
))
varCategories[, varOrder := .I]

## all columns in the data; any not listed above appear last as "Uncategorised"
fullList <- varCategories[colSummary, on = "Variable"]
fullList[is.na(Category), `:=`(Category = "Uncategorised", varOrder = Inf)]
setorder(fullList, varOrder)
## show each category name only on its first row
fullList[duplicated(Category), Category := ""]

fullList[, .SD, .SDcols = c("Category", "Variable", "Class", "nNA", "nUnique")] |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(tabNum(), "All columns, grouped by category in the order of the sections above, with class, number of NAs and number of unique values"))
```
